desc_en: Web application for the conformance testing of IT systems against semantic and technical specifications.
long_desc:
The Interoperability Test Bed is a service offered by the European Commission’s DIGIT to facilitate the conformance testing of IT systems. The Test Bed is itself a software system that can be both downloaded and installed locally, but also reused through a shared online installation operated by DIGIT. It offers an intuitive web user interface and rich integration features that allow administrators to define their project’s overall testing setup as well as users to connect and run tests.
In terms of the testing approach it follows, the Test Bed is typically used to exchange messages with the software systems being tested, supporting both the sending and receiving of messages, validating all steps against the target specification and according to the specific scenario’s expectations. Such scenarios can focus on technical details but can also be defined at business-level, exposing details only when needed to troubleshoot failures. Furthermore, tests can be designed to cover both normal flows but also edge cases and error scenarios that would be otherwise difficult to replicate.
name: Interoperability Test Bed
short_desc: Web application for the conformance testing of IT systems against semantic and technical specifications.
used_by: Publications Office of the European Union

desc_en: Customisable web application for the validation of CSV data via various APIs.
long_desc:
The Interoperability Test Bed's CSV validator is a web application for the validation of CSV data against Table Schemas. It supports a web user interface, as well as SOAP and REST APIs for machine-to-machine integration. It can also be (re)used as the implementation of a validation step in GITB TDL test cases, the executable test cases used in the Interoperability Test Bed for conformance testing. The validator is fully configuration-driven allowing its customisation for the needs of specific projects and organisations, ranging from the configuration of supported types of validation to its look  and feel. 
The validator is supported by the European Commission's DIGIT which also provides hosting for eligible public validators on its cloud infrastructure. In such a case, operation is managed by DIGIT but the validator's configuration and updates remain fully under the control of its owner. Alternatively, the validator can also be self-hosted by using its public Docker image and providing it with the project's specific configuration.
name: Interoperability Test Bed - CSV validator
short_desc: Customisable web application for the validation of CSV data via various APIs.
used_by: Publications Office of the European Union

desc_en: Ensures that signed digital documents remain verifiable for decades
long_desc:
The PreserveEU system is a digital preservation solution to ensure the long-term validity, integrity,  and authenticity of electronically signed documents. Instead of applying multiple timestamps to  each document (as in traditional extension methods), it leverages a Merkle Tree (Hash Tree)  structure to efficiently group document hashes and preserve them collectively.
By combining cryptographic hashing and trusted timestamps, PreserveEU offers a scalable, secure,  and cost-efficient way to maintain compliance and protect digital evidence for decades.
name: PreserveEU
short_desc: Ensures that signed digital documents remain verifiable for decades

desc_en: Calculates energy needed to transform water into steam at given conditions.
features: Calculate enthalpy change for water-to-steam transformation
Support for multiple temperature and pressure units
Configurable boiler efficiency and natural gas LHV
long_desc: This tool calculates the energy requirements for water-to-steam transformation given initial and final temperature and pressure. It accounts for boiler efficiency and determines natural gas consumption. An interactive Streamlit web interface is provided.
name: Steam Energy Requirements Calculator
short_desc: Calculates energy needed to transform water into steam at given conditions.

desc_en:
Simulation tool that developed by the European Commission used for
determining CO2 emissions from Heavy Duty Vehicles.
long_desc:
VECTO is the simulation tool that has been developed by the European
Commission and is used for determining CO2 emissions and Fuel Consumption
from Heavy Duty Vehicles (trucks, buses and coaches) with a Gross Vehicle
Weight above 3500kg.

Since 1 January 2019, the tool is mandatory for new trucks under certain
vehicle categories in application to the certification legislation under
type approval. 

CO2 emissions and fuel consumption data determined with VECTO, together
with other related parameters, must be monitored and reported to the
Commission by Member States and manufacturers, and made publicly available
for each of those new trucks.

Five different mission profiles for trucks and five different mission
profiles for buses and coaches have been developed and implemented in the
tool to better reflect the current European fleet. VECTO is a downloadable
executable file designed to operate on a single computer.

The inputs for VECTO are characteristic parameters to determine the power
consumption of every relevant vehicle component. Among others, the
parameters for rolling resistance, air drag, masses and inertias, gearbox
friction, auxiliary power and engine performance are input
name: vecto-sim
short_desc:
Simulation tool that developed by the European Commission used for
determining CO2 emissions from Heavy Duty Vehicles.
